data: Gender, Masculinity and the Languages of Grief

This course explores grief as a political emotion and examines how gender is constituted in response to loss. Using a range of texts that draw upon literature, psychoanalysis, and anthropology—including traditions of lament and dirges across cultures, as well as ancient and modern literature on grief, and explorations of gendered modes of grief historically available to men and women—it offers insights into how men and women are socially expected to process loss and perform mourning. The course invites reflection on how such performances, both in everyday and eventful contexts, whether aligned with or at variance with social expectations, enable the articulation of divergent political imaginaries and possible futures that could potentially disrupt the dominant order of things.
Assistant Professor, Sociology and Social Anthropology
